positive.reasoning: Criterion A1 (traumatic event): MET — patient described a threatening incident occurring six months ago. Criterion B1 (re-experiencing): MET — patient reports distressing memories almost daily and unsettling dreams. Criterion B2 (avoidance of thoughts): MET — patient consistently avoids reminders and discussions about the event. Criterion B3 (avoidance of reminders): MET — patient avoids places and conversations related to the event almost daily. Criterion C1 (inability to recall details): MET — patient struggles to remember important parts of the trauma regularly. Criterion C2 (negative beliefs): MET — patient feels more critical of the world and others almost daily. Criterion C3 (self-blame): MET — patient frequently blames themselves in an unreasonable manner. Criterion C4 (negative emotional state): MET — patient reports consistently negative feelings since the event. Criterion C5 (anhedonia): MET — patient has lost interest in activities they previously enjoyed. Criterion C6 (detachment): MET — patient feels detached from others and prefers isolation. Criterion C7 (inability to experience positive feelings): MET — patient finds it difficult to experience good feelings consistently. Criterion D1 (irritability): MET — patient reports increased irritability and outbursts. Criterion D2 (recklessness): MET — patient engages in impulsive driving behavior frequently. Criterion D3 (hypervigilance): MET — patient is more alert and finds it hard to relax. Criterion D4 (startle response): MET — patient is more easily startled several times a week. Criterion D5 (concentration difficulties): MET — patient has difficulty focusing most days. Criterion D6 (sleep disturbances): MET — patient experiences difficulty sleeping most nights. Criterion E (duration): MET — symptoms began shortly after the traumatic event and have persisted for more than one month. Criterion F (functional impairment): MET — patient reports significant distress and interference with work and relationships. Criterion G (exclusion): NOT MET — patient denies substance use or medical conditions that could explain symptoms. Total: 14 of 14 criteria met (threshold ≥ 1). Diagnosis: TRUE — full criteria for PTSD are met with significant functional impairment confirmed.
